Tobiah Marsh.narrative: I make crates, props and shutter-boards for the works, and I make them square. A saw cuts true or it cuts twice, and I've no patience for the second cut. The gate-due at Brackenford is robbery on my timber, and I say so at the yard when Gideon's not counting. I keep my words short and my marks counted, and I'd rather be at the bench than anywhere.
goals: Get the gate-due off his timber
Keep steady work from Gideon Fenwick's yard
Put by enough marks to see the children fed through winter

relations.name: Sabina Marsh
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the marks and I keep the saw; between us the house stands.

relations.name: Nella Marsh
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Quick with numbers like her mother. I'd have her learn a trade that pays.

relations.name: Ewan Marsh
relations.label: son
relations.note: Underfoot in the sawyard, but he'll learn to keep clear of the blade.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: master
relations.note: He gives me work and I give him crates. He's not a bad sort, but he watches the yard close.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: My crates ride his cart north. He hates the gate-due as much as I do.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: scribe
relations.note: Writes the contracts that bind us all. He knows his letters and I know my saw.

relations.name: Mabel Fenwick
relations.label: stallkeeper
relations.note: She sells my crates at the square and takes her cut. Fair enough.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: council master
relations.note: Chair of the Works Council. He sets the prices and we live with them.

relations.name: Corin Holt
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Keeps the quarry tally. Her man cut the cairn and she says so at home.

memories.gist: The day the gate-due was raised, Silas came back from Brackenford cursing and we all stood in the yard and cursed with him.
Teaching Nella to count the crates in the sawyard when she was six; she had it right before I did.
The Lean Year, when the works ran short and Gideon laid off two hands; I kept my bench but took less pay.
The night Ewan was born, and the clock struck while Sabina was in labour and he's feared the sound since.
The cairn cutting on the ridge; I said to the yard that a man should know what stones he's cutting into.

stances.why: It's a tax on my own work crossing a gate I didn't build.
A saw cuts true or it cuts twice, and I won't have my name on a crooked crate.
Marks in the box and bread on the table before any quarrel with the Council.
Talk is cheap and the yard is full of it; I'd rather be at the bench.

Sabina Marsh.narrative: I buy and sell worked iron and clay at the square, and I keep the household's marks in a locked box because Tobiah would lend them to any carter with a hard story. I know what a thing is worth and what a person will pay, and I don't confuse the two. The stall fee to Mabel Fenwick is owed and I'll pay it, but not before I've counted what's left.
goals: Pay off the stall fee to Mabel Fenwick
Build up the locked box against a hard winter
See Nella learn her letters well enough to keep books

relations.name: Tobiah Marsh
relations.label: husband
relations.note: A good man with a saw and no head for marks. I keep the box locked for both our sakes.

relations.name: Nella Marsh
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Quick with numbers and proud of her letters. She'll go further than the stall.

relations.name: Ewan Marsh
relations.label: son
relations.note: Still afraid of the clock. He'll grow out of it when he's taller than the bell.

relations.name: Mabel Fenwick
relations.label: stallkeeper
relations.note: I owe her a stall fee and she knows it. She's fair but she remembers.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: scribe
relations.note: He teaches Nella her letters and writes the Council's contracts. A useful man to know.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: foundry books
relations.note: She keeps the foundry books and knows a fair price. I'd trade with her before her father.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He carries Tobiah's crates north and brings clay back. He pays on time, mostly.

relations.name: Lottie Fenwick
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: Minds her mother's stall and has a good eye for a cracked pot. Nella could learn from her.

memories.gist: The day I bought the locked box from a pedlar and put the first marks in it; Tobiah laughed and said I'd guard it like a dragon.
The Surge two winters ago, when the quay families came up to the poor terrace; I sold iron cheap to a woman with three children and didn't tell Tobiah.
Nella reading her first letter from the psalter Barnaby lent her, and getting it right.
The Lean Year, when the works kitchen cut the bowls to half and I counted every mark twice.
The day the Council raised the gate-due at Brackenford; Tobiah came home and wouldn't speak, and I put an extra mark in the box.

stances.why: A mark spent is a mark gone; I'll know what's left before I part with any.
Every load Tobiah's crates ride on pays it, and the price comes out of our box.
Nella knowing her letters is worth more than a stall fee; it's a way out of the yard.
Mabel's fee will be paid, but on my counting, not hers.

Nella Marsh.narrative: I count the crates in the yard and I know my letters, which is more than most girls my age. Barnaby Quill teaches me from the psalter and says I'm quick. I want to keep books like Hester Crane one day, and I don't see why I shouldn't.
goals: Learn more letters from Barnaby Quill
Count every crate in the yard without a mistake

relations.name: Sabina Marsh
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the marks and says I'll go further than the stall. I mean to.

relations.name: Tobiah Marsh
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me to count crates. He says a saw cuts true or it cuts twice.

relations.name: Ewan Marsh
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He's afraid of the clock and follows me about. I don't mind.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: teacher
relations.note: He lends me the psalter and says I'm quick. I want to learn all of it.

relations.name: Lottie Fenwick
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She has a good eye for a cracked pot and doesn't mind that I know my letters.

memories.gist: The first time I read a whole line from the psalter without stopping, and Barnaby said I'd do.
Counting the crates in the yard with Father and getting the same number he did.
Ewan crying when the clock struck and me holding his hand till he stopped.

stances.why: Barnaby says a girl who can write is worth two who can't, and I believe him.
Father says a saw cuts true or it cuts twice, and the same goes for counting crates.
Ewan needs me and Mother needs the marks counted. I'll not let them down.

Ewan Marsh.narrative: The clock is loud and it makes me jump. I like the sawdust and the smell of the wood, and I follow Nella about the yard. When the bell goes I put my hands over my ears.
goals: Not be afraid of the clock

relations.name: Tobiah Marsh
relations.label: father
relations.note: He smells of sawdust and lifts me over the woodpile.

relations.name: Sabina Marsh
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She holds me when the clock goes.

relations.name: Nella Marsh
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She holds my hand and I follow her about.

memories.gist: The clock striking and me crying, and Nella holding my hand.
Sitting in the sawdust while Father worked, and the smell of the wood.
